Travel & Stay

Getting to Markree

How to reach us in the west of Ireland, and where to stay nearby.

The easiest way

Fly to Knock, forty minutes from Markree

Ireland West Airport Knock has direct flights from London Heathrow, Stansted and Luton, and from Manchester, Liverpool, Birmingham, East Midlands and Edinburgh. From the airport, a taxi will have you at Markree in about forty minutes.

  • Via DublinAbout 2½ hours by car, or around 3 hours by train to Collooney, the village beside Markree.
  • From BelfastAbout 3 hours by car, through Enniskillen.

The address
Markree Castle, Collooney, Co. Sligo F91 AE81

Directions
  • Flights to Knock run a few times a day, so they're worth booking once your plans are set.

Markree

Markree Castle

A castle on the banks of the River Unshin, in the heart of County Sligo.

Markree had us from the very first visit: light falling through stained glass onto the grand staircase, a dining room made for long evenings, and Fionn, the castle's resident wolfhound, presiding over it all. It is a house that deserves to be full of the people we love.

Over the course of the day, we'll drift through its halls, up its stairs and into its firelit corners, glass in hand, as the castle becomes a mixing pot of every chapter of our lives. We can hardly wait.

Where
Collooney, Co. Sligo
Since
1663
The river
The Unshin

Its story

Three and a half centuries in the making.

  1. 1663

    A fort on the river

    The Cooper family were granted Markree and its lands. It began life as a fort, guarding a ford on the River Unshin.

  2. 1727

    Forty thousand acres

    By now the estate had grown to some forty thousand acres, and the old fort had become a comfortable manor house.

  3. Early 1800s

    A castle is born

    The architect Francis Johnston, who also designed Dublin's General Post Office, reimagined the house as the castle you'll see today.

  4. 1834

    Stars over Sligo

    An observatory in the grounds held the largest refracting telescope in the world. In 1848, astronomers here discovered the asteroid Metis.

  5. 1881

    The coldest night

    On 16 January, Markree recorded −19.1°C. It's still the coldest temperature ever measured in Ireland.

  6. 2017

    A new chapter

    After more than three centuries with the Coopers, the castle was carefully restored by the Corscadden family and opened its doors again.

  7. 2027

    Hannah & Lawrence

    On Saturday 18 September, we're married here, surrounded by the people we love. And you become part of Markree's story too.

The estate

Beyond the castle walls lie sweeping lawns, box-hedged gardens and old woodland, running gently down to the River Unshin. Red squirrels, otters and kingfishers make their home along its banks, and some of the oldest trees grew sideways for a time before deciding to reach for the sky. The grounds are yours to wander whenever the mood, and the weather, allows.

Make a trip of it

The Wild Atlantic Way

Sligo sits on the Wild Atlantic Way, the coast road that runs for about 2,500 kilometres down the west of Ireland, from Malin Head in Donegal to Kinsale in Cork. It’s a coastline of sea cliffs and long beaches, islands and lighthouses, small harbour towns and very good pubs.

Our celebrations run from Friday to Sunday, but if you find yourself with a little time either side of the weekend, the coast is well worth exploring. We’ve put together the map below for anyone who’s curious: a few famous spots along the route, from Slieve League and Mullaghmore just up the road from Sligo, to the Cliffs of Moher and the Skelligs further south.

Map of the Wild Atlantic Way

Safe travels, and see you in Sligo.

A little history

  1. 1

    The route itself

    Opened by Fáilte Ireland in 2014, the route runs about 2,500 km through nine counties, from Donegal to Cork. It is one of the longest defined coastal touring routes in the world.

  2. 2

    Skellig Michael

    Monks built stone beehive huts on this Atlantic rock more than a thousand years ago. It is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

  3. 3

    Carrowmore & Knocknarea

    Minutes from Markree: one of Ireland’s largest and oldest megalithic cemeteries, below the hill where Queen Maeve is said to be buried.

  4. 4

    Yeats country

    W. B. Yeats is buried at Drumcliffe under Ben Bulben, and the Lake Isle of Innisfree lies on Lough Gill.

  5. 5

    The Spanish Armada

    In 1588, ships of the Armada were wrecked on the beach at Streedagh, on the Sligo coast.

  6. 6

    Derrigimlagh

    Marconi’s transatlantic wireless station stood on this bog, and Alcock and Brown landed here after the first non-stop transatlantic flight in 1919.
